meta.descripcion: Porsche 911 Restomod developed as a comprehensive project covering the bodywork, engine, gearbox, interior, and tuning.

h1: Porsche Restomod: a classic built to be driven

parrafos: The PA10/01 is our interpretation of the perfect 911: a car built entirely in-house and unveiled in Madrid in 2025. It serves as a benchmark for the scope of a project of this kind.

imagenes.alt: The cream PA10 911 on display in the showroom, door open

secciones.titulo: What is required in the base vehicle
parrafos: A restomod reimagines a classic as a complete system to enhance its usability without losing the identity that made it the right choice in the first place.
items: The quality of the base vehicle.

imagenes.alt: Detail of the PA10's headlight and indicator, with the bonnet strap behind

secciones.titulo: A unified project, not just a collection of upgrades
parrafos: Bodywork, paint, engine, transmission, interior, and engineering are all defined within the same project. An isolated improvement must not shift the problem to another component.
Decisions are made regarding which character traits should remain and which limitations need correcting. Top speed alone rarely defines a car as enjoyable, reliable, and usable.

secciones.titulo: What is preserved from a classic
parrafos: A restomod that fixes everything ceases to be the car one originally sought to preserve.
items: The engine's character, even if the output figures change.
The driving position and the connection with the car.
The identity of the bodywork, even when rebuilt.
The features that make that generation recognizable compared to the next.
Decisions are made and documented regarding what is *not* preserved; nothing is simply lost along the way.

parrafos: The Magazine showcases the work and photographs of this documented case.

imagenes.alt: Front of the cream PA10 911, with the fibreglass bumper and amber indicators

secciones.titulo: A classic that can actually be driven
parrafos: A restomod is neither a restoration nor a customization. A restoration returns the car to its factory-fresh state; a customization involves swapping parts on a car that remains fundamentally the same vehicle. A restomod takes a classic base and completely rebuilds it to drive like a modern car, while preserving the lines and character of the original.

It is a project that brings together all the company's in-house capabilities at once: bodywork and paint, engine shop, transmission, upholstery, and project engineering. That is why there are so few of them, and why the specifications for each one are defined with the client before any work begins.

secciones.titulo: Tested and documented as a complete package
parrafos: A unique unit developed to its own specific configuration, tested and documented as a complete package rather than a collection of independent modifications.
Depending on the car's condition and the project goals, work can be coordinated with the PA10/01, design and engineering team, and the engine shop.

secciones.titulo: How does it differ from a restoration?
parrafos: Restoration aims to return a car to a previous specification; a restomod starts with a classic car to create a new specification. Both require rigor, but they pursue different outcomes.
The PA10/01 demonstrates capability and design philosophy. Each new project must reflect its owner and its base vehicle, so the definition process begins anew based on intended use.
